newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares end week mixed in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares end week mixed in active trade.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares ended the week mixed in active trade with brokers predicting the key index would come off next week on continued foreign profit-taking.
"The market generally looks a bit soft at the moment," one dealer said.
"Most foreign investors are taking their profits and I think the index will come off next week," he said.

Counters to advance on Friday included pork producer Colcom, tyre manufactureer Dunlop and Radar, all five cents up at 385, 180 and 205 respectively. Ariston put on 40 cents to 1,540 and Delta gained 50 cents to 3,250.

Paper and packaging firm Hunyani and seed company Seedco were both five cents down at 350 and 190 respectively, tobacco concern TSl shed 20 cents to 600 and timber producer Border and sugar grower Hippo both went 25 cents down to 1,325 and 900 respectively.

Financial group Finhold shed 40 cents to 950 and wine and food processors Cairns eased 50 cents to 1,050. Bankers Barclays and multi industrial IHL were both unchanged in reasonable turnover. The 57-share industrial index closed at 7,977.24, a 68.51 point loss on the week.

Minings were quiet with nickel producer Bindura and gold miners Rio Tinto both at previous levels while Falgold added five cents to 135 and Ashanti lost 500 cents 13,000, pushing the seven-counter index down to 1230.89, a 1.44 point decline on the week.
